cards.front: Why does fractional distillation separate crude oil into different fractions?
cards.back: Hydrocarbons have different **boiling points**, so each vapour condenses at its own height in the column, and hydrocarbons with similar boiling points collect together.
cards.hint: Think about what changes from the bottom of the column to the top.

cards.front: What general formula describes every alkane?
cards.back: $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$, where $n$ is the number of carbon atoms in one molecule.
cards.hint: Compare the formulas of methane and ethane.

cards.front: How does increasing hydrocarbon chain length affect boiling point and volatility?
cards.back: **Boiling point rises** and volatility falls. Longer chains also flow less easily and ignite less easily than shorter ones.
cards.hint: Link your answer to where long chains condense in the column.

cards.front: How did crude oil form from ancient organisms?
cards.back: Their remains were **buried** under layers of sediment. Over millions of years, heat and pressure changed them into oil.

cards.front: Why is crude oil not a single compound?
cards.back: It is a **mixture** of many compounds, mostly hydrocarbons, which can be separated because they have different properties.

cards.front: What are the steps of fractional distillation of crude oil?
cards.back: 1) Heat the crude oil until most of it vaporises. 2) The vapour enters a tall column that is hot at the bottom and cooler at the top. 3) Vapours rise, cool and condense at different heights. 4) Each fraction is collected.

cards.front: What is the formula of the alkane with 5 carbon atoms, using the general formula?
What does it mean for an alkane to be saturated?
cards.back: It has only single carbon–carbon bonds, so each carbon holds the **maximum** possible number of hydrogen atoms.

cards.front: What products form when an alkane burns with too little oxygen?
cards.back: **Incomplete combustion** produces carbon monoxide or carbon particles instead of carbon dioxide.
cards.hint: Compare with the products when oxygen is plentiful.

cards.front: What is a fraction in fractional distillation?
cards.back: A collected mixture of hydrocarbons with **similar boiling points**.

cards.front: What are very long-chain fractions used for?
cards.back: They are used as lubricants or for road surfacing. They have high boiling points, are less volatile and are more viscous.
cards.hint: Compare their properties with those of petrol.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to say every molecule in a fraction has the same chain length?
cards.back: Each fraction contains **several** hydrocarbons with similar boiling points, so their chain lengths vary within it.
